A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–O. Relocations and table renumbering can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original head-overlap measurements, activation-patching experiments, prompt-failure analyses, and code-generation and compositional-task results in Section 2 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including cross-prompt comparisons, causal interventions and HumanEval-X code-generation steering experiments.

M1.justification: The operational head-identification criteria and activation-patching procedures remain unchanged in Section 2.2.2 and Appendices G/J. The retrieval-head introduction replaces path-patching language with output-decoding language, but the documented identification procedure is retained. Added code-head details describe the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 17 simple tasks, three compositional tasks, number-list ambiguity scenario and HumanEval-X Python/JavaScript tasks. The added programming-language vocabulary table does not introduce new evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix I retains the same universal function-vector-head comparison, and the intervention experiments retain their baseline and related-task controls. Changes to related-work citations do not add or remove evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The model suite, prompt templates, intervention settings, metrics and 164-problem HumanEval-X evaluation remain unchanged. Section 2.5.2 newly explains application of the existing head-selection criterion to code tasks; it does not report a revised experimental setting.

E4.justification: The parameter-sensitivity studies, failure and ambiguity analyses, function-vector overlap, base-versus-instruction-model comparisons and LLM-generated vocabulary checks are retained in Appendices E, H–K and N–O. No ablation or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the existing boxplots and correlation summaries. There is no added or revised run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative examples match. Both report 73% average cross-style head overlap (Figure 3), 90% Python steering success (Section 2.5.2), and 23 Python versus 18 JavaScript heads (Figure 75). Renumbered code examples retain their outputs.

T1.justification: The formal head-selection criteria in Section 2.2.2 and Appendix J.1, and the average-activation and intervention equations in Appendix G, are unchanged. No new theorem, proof or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged. The shortened contribution summary preserves the claims that lexical task heads are shared across prompting styles and influence retrieval mechanisms, helping explain behavioral variability.

C2.justification: Section 3 replaces v1's affirmative account of privileged access and high-fidelity self-explanation with discussion acknowledging concerns about the faithfulness of activation-explanation evaluations. The paper's own mechanistic interpretations and Section 4 limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 2.5.2 explicitly describes the existing one-match/top-ten criterion for code heads, and Appendix L adds Python/JavaScript matching vocabularies, including capitalization and symbol variants. These improve reproducibility documentation; the repository destination and other technical settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 3 adds six activation-explanation references, including Patchscopes, SelfIE and LatentQA, and revises its characterization of the retained Millicent Li et al. paper. Section 5 removes the sentence citing Han, Kahardipraja and Lu (2025). The central positioning against function vectors remains.

P1.justification: Localized edits condense the contribution summary and motivation, rewrite the retrieval-head explanation, and expand code-head documentation. Code availability is moved, and proceedings, equal-contribution, funding and disclosure text is added. The scientific narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Appendix L gains a two-row vocabulary table, shifting Figure 75 downward and renumbering existing code examples from Tables 27–28 to 28–29. Main-text figures, tables and references reflow, while the existing graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit Python/JavaScript vocabularies in Appendix L reduce a concrete reproducibility gap. Section 3 also provides broader context and acknowledges faithfulness concerns about activation explanations. These are useful, limited gains; the empirical evidence and substantive applicability limitations remain unchanged.
